newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 8.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 8:

WASHINGTON - An apologetic Newt Gingrich was re-elected House speaker after a frantic lobbying campaign that convinced all but nine Republicans that his ethical violations should not deprive him of another term.
WASHINGTON - Shortly before the vote, House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Representative Constance Morella entered a private cloakroom office and talked for three minutes as an aide guarded the door.
WASHINGTON - During last year's costly Congressional campaigns, donors helped produce many a winner and Tuesday big business sponsors across town held receptions for victorious lawmakers.
WASHINGTON - In an attempt to stem the flight of businesses to the suburbs, the D.C. Council voted to reduce employers' costs for unemployment insurance by $8.9 million this year.
WASHINGTON - The 21-day strike by Teamsters union truck drivers against Giant Food Inc. has led to shortages of national brand items such as some cereals, frozen foods and canned goods.
WASHINGTON - Charles Ruff, the attorney for the D.C. government and an expert in white-collar criminal law will be the new White House counsel, President Clinton announced.
